title: How does the hub show Matt's usage?
context: Matt wants to see his plan usage, and Fable usage in particular, in the hub's visual display. The Agent SDK gives per-turn tokens and estimated cost per model (stable), and the plan limits behind /usage (5-hour, 7-day, per-model weekly windows with reset times) through a method marked experimental, plus rate_limit events. The hub keeps none of it today.

options.name: Plan meters plus per-model totals
options.summary: A hub-wide poller reads plan usage every few minutes through the experimental call and listens for rate_limit events. A usage event per turn goes into the append-only log, so totals survive restarts. The always-on strip carries 5-hour, 7-day and Fable meters, with a usage panel on click. If the experimental call fails, the meters hide quietly.
pros: Answers how close Matt is to his limits, including Fable
cons: Relies on an experimental SDK method

options.name: Per-model totals only
options.summary: Stable data only: today's and the session's tokens and estimated cost per agent and model, in a panel.
cons: No plan percentages or reset times

options.name: Limit warnings only
options.summary: No meters; an amber notice near a limit, red when work is blocked.

recommendation: It answers what Matt asked, including Fable, and the quiet fallback makes the experimental risk acceptable.

settles.value: plan meters (5-hour, 7-day, per-model incl. Fable) in the always-on strip from the SDK usage method plus rate_limit events, per-turn usage events in the log, a usage panel on click; hide quietly if the experimental call fails
